one_liner: Senior Executive Service leader at FHWA who sets national policy on highway pavements, construction practices, and contract administration for the Federal-aid highway program.
fit_summary: This is an SES position that requires executive-level experience leading surface transportation policy on pavements, materials, infrastructure design, construction management, or contract administration. Daniel's emergency-management consulting background at IEM and strong policy knowledge do not show the executive leadership or highway engineering expertise that TQ 1 and the five ECQs demand. Daniel's time is better spent on GS-level policy, outreach, or emergency-management roles.
eligibility: Open to the public and SES members; you must be a U.S. citizen or national.

You must show TQ 1: executive-level leadership in developing, implementing, or evaluating surface transportation laws, regulations, and policies on pavements, materials, construction, or contract administration.
You must demonstrate all five ECQs within a two-page resume. Separate narratives are not accepted.
The Key requirements say a Secret clearance is required, but the clearance field says Not Required. Confirm with HR, and expect a background check and fingerprinting.
If selected, your qualifications must be certified by OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board, and you would serve a one-year probationary period.
strategy: Be honest with yourself: apply only if your IEM role included executive-level leadership of transportation or infrastructure policy, which is not on file.
If you apply, address every ECQ and TQ 1 inside two pages, with a short labeled accomplishment for each, because separate narratives are not reviewed.

Frame IEM work around contract administration, consultant services, and federal grant or program compliance (for example, FEMA Public Assistance infrastructure projects) only if you actually did that work.
Use ECQ 1 to show your deep knowledge of the American system of government and constitutional principles. This is your genuine strength.
Better use of effort: target GS-11/12/13 FHWA, FEMA, or DOT roles in program analysis, intergovernmental affairs, or public engagement, where your background is competitive.
The deadline is 11:59 PM Eastern on November 20, 2026. Prepare for a possible writing sample and a scenario-based presentation.
resume_bullets: Led [team size/scope] on [infrastructure or recovery program] for [government client], managing [budget] and delivering [result] against client goals.
Advised [state/local agency] on [federal regulation or contract administration requirement], producing [policy, guidance, or process] adopted by [number] jurisdictions.
Identified [process inefficiency] in [program] and implemented [change], reducing [cost/time] by [amount].
interview_questions: Describe a time you led development of a national or statewide policy on infrastructure or construction standards.
How have you cut wasteful spending or improved efficiency in a program you led?
How would you hold staff accountable while leading an organization through change?
How would you oversee states' construction contracting under the Federal-aid highway program to ensure compliance?
watch_outs: This is an SES role requiring proven executive and highway technical leadership, so qualification is very unlikely without both.
The two-page limit is strictly enforced; content past page 2 will not be reviewed, or the resume may be disqualified.
The clearance requirement is contradictory in the posting, and the SES probationary period ends in termination unless the agency certifies your continued employment in writing.
